title: Review: Angular momentum and its conservation; Simple harmonic motion: definition and graphs; Mass–spring and pendulum; SHM with calculus and physical pendulum
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: O01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; O02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; O02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; R06-ap2#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: O01-1#N.11, O02-1#N.4b, O05-calc-1#N.4, R06-ap2#N.9, O05-calc-1#N.3, R06-ap2#N.6, O05-calc-1#N.9, O05-calc-1#N.7, O05-calc-1#N.13a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Equilibrium position
items.clue: Place where an oscillating object would rest; the restoring force is zero there.

items.label: Pendulum
items.clue: Its period is longer with a longer string and is unchanged by the mass of the bob.

items.label: Mass–spring system
items.clue: Oscillator whose period is shorter when stiffer and is unchanged by g and by amplitude.

items.label: Elliptical orbit
items.clue: Satellite path on which K and U trade while E and L stay constant; fastest when closest.

questions.stem: A pendulum bob swings to and fro in a small arc. At the lowest point of its swing, what are its acceleration along its path and its speed?

options.text: Acceleration along the path greatest; speed zero.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed greatest.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed also zero.
Acceleration along the path greatest; speed greatest.

questions.explanation: The lowest point is equilibrium: the restoring force along the path is zero there. The bob sped up all the way down and starts to slow on the way up, so its speed is greatest here.

questions.stem: A block attached to an ideal spring oscillates on a horizontal surface with negligible friction, with period T. The block is replaced by a block with 4 times the mass, and the new block is set oscillating with 3 times the original amplitude. The new period is how many times T?
The position of an object in SHM is x = A cos(ωt + φ). At t = 0 the object is at x = +A/2 and is moving in the +x direction. What is φ?

Car 1, of mass m, drives at constant speed v along a straight road that passes a lamp post at a perpendicular distance d. Car 2, of mass 2m, drives at constant speed v/2 along a straight road that passes the same post at a perpendicular distance 3d. What is the ratio L₂/L₁ of the magnitudes of the cars' angular momenta about the post?
questions.explanation: L = mv r⊥. Car 1: mvd. Car 2: 2m × (v/2) × 3d = 3mvd. Ratio 3, the same at every point of each road.

questions.stem: A particle of mass m moves along the x-axis. The only force exerted on it is a conservative force for which the system's potential energy is U(x) = βx², where β is a positive constant. Applying Newton's second law gives an equation of the form d²x/dt² = −ω²x. What is the period T of the motion?

A lump of clay moving horizontally in a straight line strikes and sticks to the outer edge of a door that is initially at rest. The door can rotate about vertical hinges with negligible friction. The collision decreases the kinetic energy of the clay–door system. Which statement about the angular momentum of the clay–door system about the hinge axis is correct?

options.text: It decreases, since the system's kinetic energy decreases.
It is the same just after the collision as it was just before.
It increases from zero, as the clay moved in a straight line.
It changes, because the hinges exert a force on the door.

questions.stem: A torsion pendulum consists of a horizontal uniform disk suspended from a vertical wire attached to its center. The disk undergoes small rotational oscillations about the wire, for which Iα = −kΔθ. Which single change would increase the period of the oscillations?

options.text: Replacing the disk with a thin ring of equal mass and radius
Twisting the disk through a larger angle before it is released
Taking the apparatus to a location where the value of g is smaller
Replacing the disk with a heavier one of the same rotational inertia

questions.stem: A uniform disk of radius R = 0.10 m hangs from a fixed horizontal axle that passes through a point on its rim, perpendicular to the face of the disk. The rotational inertia of a uniform disk of mass M about an axis through its center, perpendicular to its face, is (1/2)MR². The disk is displaced through a small angle and released. What is the period of its oscillations? Use g = 10 m/s².

A pendulum consists of a light rigid rod of length L, pivoted about a fixed horizontal axis through its upper end, with two small objects, each of mass m, fastened to it: one at a distance L/4 from the axis and one at the rod's lower end. For small angular displacements θ, the small-angle approximation and Newton's second law in rotational form give d²θ/dt² = −ω²θ. What is ω? g is the acceleration due to gravity.
